chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who visits the House before shaving. He said, "It is not proper unless he has forgotten."

Then he said, "Some people came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله on the Day of Sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered; and some of them said: I shaved before I cast the pebbles. They did not leave anything they were supposed to do earlier except that they delayed it, and nothing they were supposed to delay except that they advanced it. So he said: There is no harm."

key_terms.أَرْمِيَ: to cast the pebbles in the hajj rite of ramy
key_terms.لَا حَرَجَ: there is no blame or hardship; no harm in the matter
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: having forgotten; forgetfulness as an excusing condition
key_terms.يَحْلِقَ: to shave the head as part of the hajj ritual sequence
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلنَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during hajj
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتَ: the Ka'bah, i.e., the Sacred House visited in hajj rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on visiting the Ka'bah before shaving during hajj if the order of rituals is changed?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the order of hajj rites, specifically visiting the Ka'bah before shaving the head. The Imam عليه السلام indicates that doing so is not proper except in the case of forgetfulness, and then cites the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who excused mistakes in the sequence of rites on the Day of Sacrifice by saying, "There is no harm."
